rows.expected: Visible wake is not advertised after notification denial; ordinary direct and mailbox delivery remain usable and delivery state is unchanged.
A native token change produces fresh per-contact capabilities, queues revocation of the former set, and never exposes either token in evidence.
The documented platform limitation is observed without a delivery claim; queued work remains durable until a later execution opportunity.
Background-only capability is revoked while Background App Refresh is unavailable; a static visible profile remains optional and ordinary delivery is unaffected.
Normal-priority background wake may be delayed; generic visible high priority is static and user-visible, and bounded continuation never becomes an unbounded foreground loop.
FCM deprioritization or delayed delivery leaves mailbox/direct retry authoritative and does not advance sent or delivered state.
Native-provider refusal or blackhole is reduced to optional wake failure; ciphertext, retries, and authenticated receipts retain their ordinary semantics.
A committed capability remains usable across an ordinary gateway restart and a revoked capability remains revoked; no stale-state restore is used.
Duplicate/flood triggers stay within gateway quotas and generic responses; the device receives no sender- or message-specific notification data.
Multiple accepted envelopes inside the coalescing window produce at most the bounded destination wake shape while every envelope remains independently receipted.
The received provider payload is exactly one documented static background or generic-visible shape with no sender, account, conversation, message, media, unread, or timestamp field.
Provider/gateway acceptance and app wake never advance queued, sent, or delivered; only existing next-hop rules and an authenticated end-to-end receipt do.
